# DistantHorizonsSupportPumpkin

<!-- docs:begin summary -->
<!-- Generated by pumpkin-plugins-docs. Edit src/info.ts, then run `pnpm readme`. -->

This unofficial integration lets Java players use Distant Horizons with terrain from your Pumpkin server.
<!-- docs:end summary -->

<!-- docs:begin reference -->
<!-- Generated by pumpkin-plugins-docs from package, action, extension, and component docs metadata. Run `pnpm readme`. -->

See the [plugin guide](https://filiphsps.github.io/pumpkin-plugins/packages/distant-horizons-support-pumpkin/docs/) and [API reference](https://filiphsps.github.io/pumpkin-plugins/api/plugins/distant-horizons-support-pumpkin/) on the documentation site.
<!-- docs:end reference -->

## Installation

Download `distant-horizons-support-pumpkin.wasm` from the plugin's GitHub release, put it in your server's `plugins/` folder, and restart Pumpkin. On the first load, a full restart lets Pumpkin ask for the plugin's permissions; hot reload cannot prompt for them.

## Permissions

<!-- docs:begin permissions -->
<!-- Generated by pumpkin-plugins-docs. Edit src/info.ts, then run `pnpm readme`. -->

Pumpkin asks for these on the server console the first time the plugin loads.

| Permission | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `fs.read.data` | Read settings and cached LOD terrain. |
| `fs.write.data` | Write settings and persist captured LOD terrain. |
| `http.outbound` | Check Pumpkin Market for plugin updates. |
<!-- docs:end permissions -->

## Configuration

<!-- docs:begin config -->
<!-- Generated by pumpkin-plugins-docs. Edit src/info.ts, then run `pnpm readme`. -->

Settings live in `plugins/data/DistantHorizonsSupportPumpkin/config.toml`. The plugin creates the file if needed, adds settings from the schema and removes settings no longer defined there. Values for existing settings are preserved.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `support.server_key` | string | `""` | Optional globally unique server key. Empty uses the client connection address. |
| `support.render_distance` | integer | `128` | Maximum LOD request radius in chunks, limited by the world border. |
| `support.generation_requests_per_second` | integer | `20` | Maximum terrain generation requests per second advertised to each DH client. DH uses this for pacing and concurrency; pending_requests also caps it. |
| `support.sync_requests_per_second` | integer | `50` | Maximum cached LOD synchronization requests per second advertised to each DH client. DH uses this for pacing and concurrency; pending_requests also caps it. |
| `support.requests_per_player` | integer | `2` | Maximum active terrain captures per player. Misses waiting for a slot and cached responses bypass this limit. |
| `support.pending_requests` | integer | `16` | Maximum in-flight DH requests and queued responses across all players. |
| `support.blocks_per_tick` | integer | `8192` | Maximum block samples per server tick across all LOD requests. Actual work adapts to server MSPT. |
| `support.packets_per_tick` | integer | `2` | Maximum transfer packets for newly captured LODs per server tick across all players. |
| `support.cached_requests_per_tick` | integer | `8` | Maximum cached LOD requests checked per server tick across all players. |
| `support.cached_packets_per_tick` | integer | `64` | Maximum transfer packets for cached LODs per server tick across all players. |
| `support.memory_cache_entries` | integer | `512` | Maximum LOD sections cached in memory. Set to 0 to disable; any negative value means unlimited. |
| `support.disk_cache_entries` | integer | `4096` | Maximum LOD sections cached on disk. Set to 0 to disable; any negative value means unlimited. |
| `support.refresh_seconds` | integer | `30` | Rebuild cached sections after this age when all their chunks are loaded. |
| `worlds."<world>".height` | integer | none | World height in blocks above its minimum Y. |
| `worlds."<world>".sample_biomes_3d` | boolean | `false` | Sample the biome at every captured height instead of using the surface biome for the whole column. Adds one world lookup per sampled block. |

<details>
<summary>A fresh install gets this file:</summary>

```toml
# DistantHorizonsSupportPumpkin configuration.
# Changes apply after a server restart. Invalid files are left untouched.

# Distant Horizons Support limits.
[support]

# Optional globally unique server key. Empty uses the client connection address.
server_key = ""

# Maximum LOD request radius in chunks, limited by the world border.
render_distance = 128

# Maximum terrain generation requests per second advertised to each DH client. DH uses this for
# pacing and concurrency; pending_requests also caps it.
generation_requests_per_second = 20

# Maximum cached LOD synchronization requests per second advertised to each DH client. DH uses this
# for pacing and concurrency; pending_requests also caps it.
sync_requests_per_second = 50

# Maximum active terrain captures per player. Misses waiting for a slot and cached responses bypass
# this limit.
requests_per_player = 2

# Maximum in-flight DH requests and queued responses across all players.
pending_requests = 16

# Maximum block samples per server tick across all LOD requests. Actual work adapts to server MSPT.
blocks_per_tick = 8192

# Maximum transfer packets for newly captured LODs per server tick across all players.
packets_per_tick = 2

# Maximum cached LOD requests checked per server tick across all players.
cached_requests_per_tick = 8

# Maximum transfer packets for cached LODs per server tick across all players.
cached_packets_per_tick = 64

# Maximum LOD sections cached in memory. Set to 0 to disable; any negative value means unlimited.
memory_cache_entries = 512

# Maximum LOD sections cached on disk. Set to 0 to disable; any negative value means unlimited.
disk_cache_entries = 4096

# Rebuild cached sections after this age when all their chunks are loaded.
refresh_seconds = 30

# Per-world terrain capture settings. Vanilla dimensions use their standard heights; unknown
# dimensions require a height override.
#
# [worlds."world"]
# height = 384  # World height in blocks above its minimum Y.
# sample_biomes_3d = false  # Sample the biome at every captured height instead of using the surface biome for the whole column. Adds one world lookup per sampled block.
```

## Compatibility and terrain

<!-- docs:begin compatibility -->
<!-- Generated by pumpkin-plugins-docs. Edit src/info.ts, then run `pnpm readme`. -->

Targets Distant Horizons **3.3.4**, using network protocol 16 on Java Edition. Bedrock players do not open DH sessions. Install the Distant Horizons client mod separately. A client using another DH protocol is disconnected with an incompatibility message. The protocol format follows [Distant Horizons core 3.3.4](https://gitlab.com/distant-horizons-team/distant-horizons-core/-/tree/3.3.4).
<!-- docs:end compatibility -->

<!-- docs:begin terrain -->
<!-- Generated by pumpkin-plugins-docs. Edit src/info.ts, then run `pnpm readme`. -->

The plugin builds LOD sections covering 64 × 64 blocks across 16 server chunks. All 16 chunks must be ready through the server terrain adapter before sampling and remain available for each capture attempt. When the optional Pumpkin++ provider is available, the plugin requests chunk preparation asynchronously; it still reads terrain through Pumpkin’s existing world adapter. Without a usable provider, the plugin captures only terrain already available to that adapter. Uncached requests stay pending while provider jobs advance across ticks; local availability failures retry with exponential backoff until terrain is ready or the client cancels. Genuinely empty terrain remains valid. By default, each vertical column uses its surface biome. Set `sample_biomes_3d = true` under that world in `[worlds."<world>"]` to sample cave and other vertical biomes; this adds a biome lookup for each sampled block. Player edits, crop growth and fire spread invalidate affected cached sections. Mutations without exact world and changed-position data from the pinned Pumpkin API may remain cached until refresh. Captures are limited to 131072 material segments per section, transfer packets carry at most 30000 data bytes; finite-bandwidth fragments fit within a 20-second credit window including the 13-byte protocol overhead; a finite client bandwidth bucket can accumulate one 30013-byte DH fragment message.
<!-- docs:end terrain -->

The plugin captures material changes, caves, biomes and lighting through Pumpkin's world-level
terrain adapter, so a multi-tick capture does not depend on short-lived chunk handles. Air above the
heightmap is collapsed without reading every empty block. When Pumpkin++ is available, ordinary
requests, `/dhs generate` and `/dhs cache recover` can ask it to prepare chunks asynchronously and
poll progress across server ticks. The plugin still samples through the terrain adapter: capture
starts only after it reports the section ready, then uses the usual `LodBuilder`. Without a usable
provider, capture uses terrain already available through the adapter.

Completed sections use the configured memory and disk cache limits independently. Disk entries
survive restarts. See [Configuration](#configuration) for the current limits and how to disable each
cache tier. When upgrading from an earlier version, the old shared cache limit is copied to both
new limits. An uncached section can take many ticks to finish. The plugin polls provider jobs on later
ticks and does not sample while the terrain adapter reports unavailable chunks. If preparation or a
terrain check fails, the request stays pending and retries with exponential backoff. Pending requests
count toward the configured queue limit. Without a usable provider, bring the area into range through
normal play or use a server chunk-loading tool. Cached sections can still be sent while their chunks
are unloaded.

An empty cache entry can represent terrain that really contains only air, so the plugin leaves it in
place. Older entries do not record whether their source chunks were loaded, so the plugin cannot
safely identify these entries as corrupt.

To rebuild one selected server cache entry, run `/dhs cache recover <x> <z>` as a Java player, using
block coordinates in the current world. Recovery runs asynchronously. The selected DHP1 entry stays
in the active cache while chunk preparation and the terrain adapter check all 16 chunks. Once they
are ready, the plugin backs up the entry under `cache-recovery/`, records its key in the matching
`.dhm` file, removes only that section from the active cache and starts a forced capture. If
preparation cannot complete, the good cache entry is left in place. Backups remain in the plugin
data directory and are not pruned automatically. Recovery changes only the server plugin cache; it
does not edit a client profile or cache. If chunks unload after the backup, it remains and the forced
capture will not save fallback air for that section.

The generated [Commands](#commands) section lists cache inspection, clearing and recovery commands,
along with the LOD map and forced-capture commands. Run `/dhs map` to see cached sections around
your position, or `/dhs map <x> <z>` to inspect block coordinates in the current world. Add
`<radius>` after the command or coordinates to choose a radius, up to 16,384 sections. At radii up
to 10, each map cell represents one 64 × 64 block LOD section (four by four server chunks). Larger
views are downsampled to 21 × 21 cells so they fit in Minecraft chat. Map commands need a player to
identify the current world.

Run `/dhs generate` or `/dhs generate <x> <z>` to force a capture into the cache. Add `<radius>`
after the command or coordinates to select up to 31 sections from the center. Each request can
select at most 4,096 sections; radius 31 selects 3,969. The job checks up to 64 cached sections per
tick, skipping valid entries. If every requested section is already cached, the plugin reports that
no capture is needed. Only one forced job can run at a time. It gets up to 32,768 block samples per
tick and pauses ordinary capture sampling while it runs, but cached-response delivery and transfers
continue. The plugin reports progress in chat about every 10%, and `/dhs status` shows the active
job. Forced capture uses the same optional Pumpkin++ preparation and terrain adapter as ordinary
requests. Without a usable provider, it skips sections whose chunks are unavailable.

For ordinary captures, `blocks_per_tick` sets the maximum sample batch. The controller adjusts each
batch using Pumpkin's reported MSPT and the measured cost of earlier capture steps, reserving 5 ms;
it allows no samples at 45 reported MSPT. On the pinned Pumpkin release, MSPT is measured before
tick-end handlers, so this reserve does not cap the plugin's full handler cost. These limits remain
provisional until the real-runtime comparison is complete. Cached LOD transfers continue while
sampling is paused. `/dhs status` reports the capture budget, reported MSPT, this handler's last
elapsed time, logical queued response bytes retained and DH packet bytes sent.

Even at zero sample budget, uncached requests get a bounded availability check. If chunks are
unavailable, the request stays pending and checks back off exponentially. If they are loaded, the
request remains queued until sampling can resume. Partially built requests check availability again
before resuming. These checks use the `cached_requests_per_tick` limit.

Finite client bandwidth settings control fragment size. At 1 KB/s, a full DH fragment message uses
at most 20,000 bytes of credit, including its 13-byte protocol envelope. This leaves 10 seconds of
margin before the DH client's 30-second receiver-buffer expiry. If the client changes its rate, the
plugin resizes unsent fragments. While a finite-rate transfer has an in-progress receiver buffer,
the server finishes it before sending another response to the same client; other clients continue
receiving round-robin service. Cancelling a queued transfer discards it and releases its retained
payload.

When a cached section reaches its configured refresh age, the plugin rebuilds it if all its chunks
are loaded. Otherwise, it returns the previous capture. Block placement and breaking invalidate the
affected server cache; crop growth and fire spread do too. Other world changes may remain cached
until refresh when Pumpkin's pinned API does not provide the exact world and changed position. Live
push updates are disabled, but clients can synchronize cached terrain on login. After replacing a
world or changing its height, stop the server and delete the plugin's cache folder. Vanilla world
heights are assumed unless you configure an override.

## Diagnosing pending requests

`/dhs status` reports worker ticks, capture progress, the sample budget, reported MSPT, the last
tick-end handler elapsed time, queued responses and logical bytes retained, DH packet bytes sent,
and served, rejected and cancelled request counts. Counts are cumulative since the plugin loaded. On
the pinned server release, Pumpkin's MSPT excludes this tick-end handler. Its Pumpkin++ provider
line reports `available`, `missing`, `incompatible` or `temporarily unreachable`. Pumpkin's standard
`ipcSend` cannot distinguish a missing recipient from other transport errors, so it reports
`temporarily unreachable` unless absence is positively confirmed. Any loaded plugin that can send host
IPC to Pumpkin++ can call it; the host-supplied sender name scopes operation IDs, leases and quotas.

The DH client's ETA measures time since request submission, including time spent waiting in a queue;
it does not measure network throughput. `Chunk ... is not loaded` means the requested terrain is
unavailable to capture. `LOD request limit reached` means the bounded request queue is full. A
configuration change gets separate generation and sync acknowledgements, and the server response
also includes the client's bandwidth limit for outgoing transfers. A bandwidth value of zero means
unlimited.

Pending requests can persist while the client keeps submitting new sections. Increasing worker ticks
and capture progress show that the worker is advancing. Increasing rejections with `Chunk ... is not
loaded` means the requested sections are still unavailable. Previously captured sections can still
be served from cache, including during a forced capture. If worker ticks stay at zero, the worker is
not being dispatched. Increasing cancellations mean the client is discarding requests. See
[troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md#requests-stay-pending-because-terrain-is-unavailable) for
ways to make the requested chunks available.
